questions.q: Which type should hold a whole number up to 10^18?
questions.e: int only reaches about 2.1 × 10^9. long long reaches about 9.2 × 10^18.
'A' is 65, so 'A' + 2 is 67, which is stored in a char and printed as the letter C.
In C++ the remainder takes the sign of the first number, so -7 % 3 is -1. For a non-negative remainder use ((a % b) + b) % b.

o: Decimals are stored with tiny rounding errors
questions.e: Most decimals can't be stored exactly in binary. Compare with a tolerance: fabs(x - y) < 1e-9.
1LL makes the multiplication happen in long long, so there is no overflow. Without it, a * b would overflow as an int.
Casting before dividing keeps the fraction (3.5). In (double)(7 / 2) the integer division has already happened, giving 3.

questions.q: What does endl do that "\n" doesn't?
questions.e: endl prints a newline and flushes the output, which is slower in big loops. "\n" only prints the newline.
